properties.name: Node-reference checking moves off the import walk and onto the whole document
properties.rationale:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 on this design's own 3388-node export: with the guard on the walk, restoring it failed with 23 faults and wrote NOTHING. Only nine were real dangling references. Three were nodes present in the SAME document at indices 3342, 3360 and 3169, referenced from 2854, 3167 and 3063 — refused because `TemporalFact` sorts before `Verification`. One was a cascade, and ten were edges orphaned by the thirteen. A design with no dangling references at all would still have failed this way, which is what makes it a class rather than this graph's data problem.

THE CAUSE: the unit of validation did not match the unit of atomicity. The import is all-or-nothing, so the document is what becomes true — and a reference must be judged against that, not against a partial state no caller ever observes. The edge guard already gets this for free by running after every node is written.

WHY REPORT RATHER THAN REFUSE, once the ordering was fixed: nine real dangles remained and the import still wrote nothing, so a graph holding ONE bad reference had an unrestorable backup, remediable only by hand-editing the export — the one thing this project tells users never to do. The write guard already stops a NEW false record being made; an import asserts nothing new, it reproduces a state that already existed. `ImportReport` had answered this exact question three times already (`skipped_edges`, `integrity_note`, `provenance_note` — all "the import still proceeds but never silently"), so this follows the house answer rather than inventing a fourth policy.

Round trip after the fix, measured: 3388/3388 nodes, 15122/15122 edges, node and edge ORDER identical, zero properties gained, dropped or changed. The export is a lossless durable artifact.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: `create_node` gained a guard refusing a property whose value NAMES a node that does not exist (the `node_ref` schema flag, for `TemporalFact.subject_id`). Correct on an interactive write, WRONG on an import: it resolved a reference against the store as it stood mid-walk, and an export is ordered by node type, never by dependency. `import_graph` now collects the references while it stages nodes and judges them AFTER every node is written, against the document's own ids plus what the graph already holds. A dangling one is REPORTED on `ImportReport.dangling_node_refs` and printed by `--import`, not refused.
